title: Timeline of history
subtitle: Three levels of detail — from ten milestones for newcomers to a detailed view of the War of the Ring.
intro: Tolkien’s chronicle of the history of Middle-earth is recorded in ages. The Second Age ended with Sauron’s fall at the gates of Mordor and the rise of the Shadow that would, in the Third Age, lead to open war. To help you orient yourself, we offer three levels of detail — pick what you need.
abbrev_post_pre: . Years are given according to Tolkien’s appendices; in some cases we round. The Lord of the Rings event takes place in our
abbrev_post_post: close to the Third Age — the exact setting differs from year to year.
lang_notice: The individual timeline entries (titles and descriptions) are currently in Czech. Translation will follow in the next update.
quick_p: Ten milestones that are enough to orient you in the story of The Lord of the Rings.
third_p: Selected milestones of the Third Age — the fall of the Northern Kingdom, the rise of Rohan, the return of the Shadow and the start of the War of the Ring.
wotr_p: A detailed breakdown of the two years in which the main story of The Lord of the Rings takes place. Dates are given according to the Gondorian calendar.
h_fourth: What changes after Sauron’s fall — the Fourth Age
fourth_p1_pre: After the destruction of the One Ring begins the
fourth_p1_post: — the age of Men. Aragorn is crowned as Elessar; the united kingdom of Gondor and Arnor is restored. Rohan and Gondor remain faithful allies.
fourth_p2: Sauron’s direct power falls. Orc bands in the mountains and in Mordor disintegrate — without a central lord they devour each other, vanish into the rocks or eventually attack only in smaller, fragmented raids. Harad and the Easterlings make truce and trade treaties with Gondor.
fourth_p3: For the elves the Fourth Age is a time of departure. The three elven rings lose their power; Galadriel, Elrond, Gildor and many others sail from the Grey Havens. Lothlórien begins slowly to fade, Rivendell loses the power of the Three. The dwarves at Erebor and the Iron Hills prosper, but Khazad-dûm remains lost.
